title.title: Zariski cancellation fails over $\mathbb{C}$
title.subtitle: Claim: one polynomial $H$ in five variables gives $A$ with $A[w] \cong \mathbb{C}^{[5]}$ but $A \not\cong \mathbb{C}^{[4]}$

plain: A shape that becomes ordinary flat space once you add one extra line, yet is not flat space itself

beats.text: Adjoining one variable makes it a polynomial ring
Yet $A$ itself is not one, so the extra line cannot be cancelled

steps: Write down one polynomial H in five variables
Add one more variable: the result is ordinary flat space
An invariant built from its symmetries shows A itself is not

achievement.label: Zariski cancellation problem
achievement.context: Before: true for complex surfaces (around 1980); false in characteristic $p$ (Gupta, 2014)
achievement.note: Here $n = 4$; dimension 3 over $\mathbb{C}$ is still open

verify.detail: Comparator states the dimension, domain and both isomorphism claims for this $H$
verify.ourCheck: We read the Comparator statement; we did not run the checker

voice.text: Is X flat space if X times a line is? Open over the complex numbers.
One polynomial: add a variable and it's flat; an invariant says it wasn't.
Claimed: false in dimension four, by one polynomial.
